articles.title: NFL teams keeping 4 quarterbacks isn't a big deal, and here's why
articles.summary: Four teams kept four quarterbacks in their final cutdown.
articles.body:
There was a question for a few NFL teams with four quarterbacks worth rostering for Week 1 about how they would handle that conundrum, considering almost every team keeps either two or three.

The answer ended up being pretty easy: Keep all four.

Four teams kept four quarterbacks on cutdown day . The reaction for some was disbelief. That's not what most teams have done, after all. (One of those teams, the Vikings, cut down to three when they released Max Brosmer on Monday afternoon, according to NFL Media .)

It makes perfect sense, though. And maybe it will become a new trend. After all, quarterback is the most important position in sports. Maybe it's time to approach it differently.

The answer for what to do with four quarterbacks was different in Cleveland. Browns second-year quarterback Dillon Gabriel, who looked very good in a preseason game on Thursday, was so injured by Sunday that he had to go on injured reserve with a back injury. How convenient.

Other teams didn't have a fourth quarterback come down with a sudden injury right before they had to make roster decisions. The Pittsburgh Steelers, Atlanta Falcons, Minnesota Vikings and Philadelphia Eagles kept four QBs on cutdown day, though the Vikings pared down to three on Monday. It's rare to see one or two teams keep that many. And the Browns magically got out of making that inevitable decision.

The easiest explanation is that the opportunity cost of keeping a fourth quarterback is low. Up to seven players are inactive on gameday in the NFL. Some of those spots are used on players who are injured and can't play that week, but there generally is an extra safety, linebacker, tight end, running back or some other position on that list. Every team believes that the rest of the league can't wait to pounce on their sixth linebacker if he is released, but that generally isn't the case. Teams can and maybe should use the 53rd spot on an extra quarterback, which has the highest potential payoff down the road if one hits.

Teams keeping four quarterbacks will still function the same. It will all work out just fine for them.

The NFL can be uncreative. It took decades for teams to feel empowered enough to go for it on fourth down in their opponents' territory. The way teams approached the preseason was the same across the league until Rams head coach Sean McVay started holding out his starters, and other teams followed. There are numerous other examples. There are few outliers when it comes to things like roster building in the NFL. Everyone does the same thing.

It's OK to think about things differently, especially if you're a franchise that hasn't won much. Keeping four quarterbacks isn't as radical as you think, but look around at some of the aghast reactions to it. That's why teams don't often go out of the box.

For something like keeping four quarterbacks, it's a very small risk to be different. In Pittsburgh, the Steelers need to figure out if they have a successor to Aaron Rodgers. For the Falcons and Eagles, their fourth quarterbacks fill a role. Atlanta's Jack Strand can be used on quarterback sneaks and maybe some other gadget plays, and Philadelphia's Cole Payton saw some snaps on special teams in the preseason.

If keeping a fourth quarterback leads a team to find its future starter or even a valuable QB2, it's much more valuable than keeping around a spare linebacker who was going to be inactive on Sundays.

articles.title: 7 Will Levis Practice Squad Landing Spots After Being Unclaimed on Waivers
articles.summary: All 32 NFL teams had to trim their rosters from 90 down to 53 or fewer on Sunday. In a […]
articles.body:
All 32 NFL teams had to trim their rosters from 90 down to 53 or fewer on Sunday. In a mild surprise, the Tennessee Titans opted to release Will Levis . On Monday, the 27-year-old quarterback passed through waivers unclaimed. Now, he'll presumably look to join another team's practice squad. But which teams could try adding the 33rd overall pick in the second round of the 2023 NFL Draft to their 16-man practice squad?

With just Josh Allen and Kyle Allen as the only two quarterbacks in the organization, the Buffalo Bills may want another arm to start learning their system. There are still a lot of traits to like about Levis, like his cannon of an arm. While Levis battles inconsistency and accuracy issues, so did the Bills' former NFL MVP. Perhaps Joe Brady and the Allens can help Levis get his career back on track.

The Cincinnati Bengals kept just Joe Burrow and Joe Flacco . Considering the latter is 41 years old, the Bengals may want to find someone to place on their practice squad now, so he can start mastering the offense. After all, an injury to either Burrow or Flacco would mean Levis is just one snap away from joining an offense that features Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. That's about as good as it gets.

Now that the Green Bay Packers traded Kyle McCord, they probably want to get another young QB for Matt LaFleur to work wonders with. Right now, all they have is a 37-year-old Tyrod Taylor backing up Jordan Love , and that's a dangerous situation should an injury occur. Levis wouldn't have to start from scratch; he already has 21 starts under his belt, so it's possible the learning curve wouldn't be as steep here.

The Tampa Bay Buccaneers ' QB room is light on experience, keeping just undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels behind Baker Mayfield , and the latter is in the final year of his contract. The Bucs may want to bridge the gap a bit by bringing in a player who's headed into his fourth season. Levis could be a weekly practice squad elevation on gameday (maybe not right away as he learns the offense), providing the Bucs with more of a veteran voice in the QB room next to Mayfield.

The Los Angeles Chargers had a training camp battle between Trey Lance and D.J. Uiagalelei, and the former No. 3 overall pick ended up winning the job, with the latter getting released. While Uiagalelei could wind up back on the taxi squad, it's possible the Chargers are enamored with the potential of Levis too. After all, he has an extremely strong arm but just needs some refinement. That's nothing new to Harbaugh, who once won a college football national championship with J.J. McCarthy .

Teddy Bridgewater 's retirement left the Detroit Lions scrambling for a new backup QB. They settled on Josh Dobbs and released undrafted rookie Luke Altmyer from the roster. Now Jared Goff and Dobbs are the only QBs in the organization. Meanwhile, Dan Campbell could grow enamored with the skill set of Levis, knowing that his big arm would play well at Ford Field, plus the Lions typically like to have a high-upside QB in development.

Perhaps the landing spot that makes the most sense for Levis is signing with the Jacksonville Jaguars . While they have two QBs on the roster in Trevor Lawrence and the recently traded Quinn Ewers, and another two on the practice squad in Nick Mullens plus Joey Aguilar, there's a special coaching connection here. The Jaguars are coached by Liam Coen, who also coached Levis at Kentucky. Yet, there's no chance a team keeps five QBs in the organization, so chances are Mullens would be the one who gets the pink slip in Duval.

articles.title: These former Green Bay Packers landed spots on 53-man NFL rosters
articles.summary: NFL rosters have a number of former Green Bay Packers. Here's a rundown.
articles.body:
Numerous former Green Bay Packers landed on rosters across the NFL when the league landed on its initial 53 players for each team following weekend cutdowns.

There is also, of course, the 53-man roster for the Green Bay Packers , including the continuation of a cool streak with an undrafted free agent on the list.

Where did former Packers end up? Here's a look:

Davante Adams, wide receiver, Los Angeles Rams

After bouncing in 2024 from the Las Vegas Raiders to the New York Jets, the former Packers star found a home last year with the Rams, catching a league-leading 14 touchdowns in only 14 games. He'll turn 34 in December.

For the last three years, he contributed to the Packers on special teams and started two games in 2024. He has five years of NFL experience.

Corey Bojorquez, punter, Cleveland Browns

The Packers' 2021 punter has been with Cleveland each of the last four seasons, leading the league in total yardage the past two.

Oren Burks, linebacker, Cincinnati Bengals

A Packer from 2018 through 2021, he's been with three other teams since but will compete for a second straight year with the Bengals. He appeared in every game in five of the past six seasons (and still appeared in 15 in 2023).

Kenny Clark, defensive tackle, Dallas Cowboys

Part of the deal that sent Micah Parsons to Green Bay last year, the three-time Pro Bowler played in 17 games for Dallas and had three sacks. He heads into his 11th season and won't turn 31 years old until October.

AJ Dillon, running back, Carolina Panthers

He played in seven games for the Philadelphia Eagles last year and has a new home after four seasons with the Packers, where he became – and remains – a fan favorite. He has 16 career NFL touchdowns.

Romeo Doubs, wide receiver, New England Patriots

Doubs was a top contributor to the Packers' pass-catching unit the past four years, starting 16 games last year and hauling in 55 receptions. In his career, he has 202 catches and 21 touchdowns, and now he begins a new chapter in the AFC after signing with New England in the offseason.

Rasul Douglas, cornerback, Washington Commanders

A key contributor to the 2021 and 2022 Packers teams before he was traded in 2023, Douglas spent last year with Miami (13 starts, 13 passes defended) after a second year in Buffalo. He just turned 31 on Aug. 29.

Kingsley Enagbare, edge rusher, New York Jets

He spent his first four seasons in Green Bay, appearing in every single game (21 starts) and racking up 11.5 career sacks. He signed a one-year deal worth $10 million with New York.

Jonathan Garvin, defensive line, Chicago Bears

Garvin has been placed on injured reserve; he hasn't appeared in an NFL game since 2022.

After seven productive seasons in Green Bay, Gary now embarks on a new journey after signing with Dallas in the offseason. He's played in 106 games with Green Bay, including 74 starts, and has 46.5 career sacks.

Nate Hobbs, cornerback, San Francisco 49ers

Hobbs battled injuries and ineffectiveness in his lone season with the Packers last year, and had been battling a groin injury in training camp. This will be his sixth NFL season.

Elgton Jenkins, offensive line, Cleveland Browns

He made two Pro Bowls as a versatile lineman with the Packers over the past seven seasons, though he was limited to nine games last year. The Browns signed him to a two-year deal worth $24 million this offseason.

Aaron Jones, running back, Minnesota Vikings

Jones, 31, appeared in 12 games for the Vikings last year and ran for 548 yards, his second season with Minnesota after rushing for 1,138 yards the year before.

Josh Myers, offensive line, New York Jets

The Packers cut ties with their starting center after four seasons following the 2024 season, and he started all 17 games for the Jets last year.

Aaron Rodgers, quarterback, Pittsburgh Steelers

For (we presume) the final time, the Packers legend will suit up for an NFL season. At age 42, he's coming off a year when he led Pittsburgh to the playoffs.

Jarran Reed, nose tackle, Seattle Seahawks

He's been with the Seahawks for nine of his 11 NFL seasons, with the 2021 campaign as a member of the Kansas City Chiefs and the 2022 season in Green Bay, where he started 14 games. He'll be 34 in December.

Micah Robinson, cornerback, Tennessee Titans

He never played for Green Bay but was a seventh-round pick in 2025. He played in nine games for Tennessee last year.

Jon Runyan Jr., offensive line, New York Giants

The guard enters his third season with the Giants, having started 19 games for them over the past two years. He played four seasons in Green Bay, starting 50 games (and three in the playoffs).

He was with the Packers from 2023 through 2025, catching eight passes and one touchdown.

Za'Darius Smith, defensive end, Atlanta Falcons

A Pro Bowler for Green Bay in 2019 and 2020, Smith walked away from football in 2025 while dealing with deaths in the family, but he's back with Atlanta after the Falcons found themselves short on pass rushers . Smith has 70.5 career sacks, including 26 with Green Bay.

Eric Stokes, cornerback, Las Vegas Raiders

Injuries kept the 2021 first-rounder from making an impact in Green Bay, but he started 16 games for the Raiders last year and came away with five passes defended and 53 tackles.

Luke Tenuta, offensive line, Indianapolis Colts

After suiting up for three games with the Packers in 2022, he returned to an NFL regular-season game last year and played in four games for the Colts.

Robert Tonyan, tight end, Pittsburgh Steelers

This will be his fifth team in five years, but he did play in all 17 for Kansas City last year. Tonyan played five years with the Packers from 2018 through 2022, catching 17 touchdown passes.

Cole Van Lanen, offensive line, Jacksonville Jaguars

The former Bay Port High School and Wisconsin Badgers alumnus spent his 2021 rookie season in Green Bay before getting traded to the Jags. Last year, he played in all 16 games (10 starts) and heads into his sixth NFL campaign.

Greg Van Roten, offensive line, New England Patriots

The guard was with the Packers in 2012 and 2013 but has remained active in the NFL since, most recently with the Giants as a starter the past two seasons. He's played in all 17 games each of the last three years.

Quay Walker, linebacker, Las Vegas Raiders

Over the past four seasons, the first-round pick started 57 games for the Packers and racked up nine sacks and 469 tackles. The Raiders signed him to a three-year deal worth more than $40 million.

Rasheed Walker, offensive line, Carolina Panthers

He's been the left tackle for the Packers over the past three seasons, a huge value for a seventh-round pick in 2022. He signed a one-year deal with the Panthers this offseason.

Dontayvion Wicks, wide receiver, Philadelphia Eagles

After three seasons in Green Bay (108 catches, 11 touchdowns), Wicks was traded in the offseason to the Eagles for draft capital.

Malik Willis, quarterback, Miami Dolphins

One of the high-profile departures of the offseason, the backup quarterback delivered excellent work for the Packers over the past two seasons before signing a three-year deal ($67.5 million) to become the Dolphins quarterback for last year's Packers defensive coordinator and now Dolphins head coach, Jeff Hafley.

Emanuel Wilson, running back, Seattle Seahawks

Over the past three seasons, he racked up 1,083 yards and seven touchdowns with the Packers, and he played in all 17 games each of the past two years. He signed a one-year deal with Seattle this offseason.

Eric Wilson, linebacker, Minnesota Vikings

The NFL veteran is on to his 10th season and second with the Vikings after playing from 2022 through 2024 in Green Bay. He started 16 games last year for Minnesota, forcing four fumbles and registering 6.5 sacks, both career highs. He'll turn 32 in September.

articles.title: Charlie Smyth: NFL's New Orleans Saints resign County Down kicker to practice squad
articles.summary: Charlie Smyth is staying with the New Orleans Saints after the County Down kicker signed to their practice squad.
articles.body:
Charlie Smyth will stay with the New Orleans Saints after the County Down kicker signed to their practice squad.

On Sunday, it was confirmed the Mayobridge man had not made the cut for a place on the NFC South franchise's 53-man squad before the start of the NFL season, and he was placed on the waiver wire.

It gave other teams the option to offer the former Gaelic footballer a contract, but that did not come to pass before Monday's 17:00 BST deadline.

Instead, Smyth will return to the Saints practice squad where he spent his entire first season and began last term, before making his debut when elevated to the full squad for a Week 13 defeat by the Miami Dolphins following Blake Grupe's release.

Smyth was also elevated in the following two weeks and a game-winning field goal against the Carolina Panthers was enough for him to earn a three-year contract for Kellen Moore's team as he saw out the season as first choice.

Last season, he made 12 of 16 field goal attempts and was perfect from 13 extra-point tries, putting him in a strong position to earn the number one slot for this season.

However, the 25-year-old had a mixed pre-season, initially facing competition from Tanner Brown before the Saints then brought in former Las Vegas Raiders' two-time All-Pro kicker Daniel Carlson whose 53-yard field goal won their final pre-season game against the Dallas Cowboys on Friday.

With Carlson winning the race for the number one spot, Smyth and Brown were waived with neither picked up by another team on Monday before the Saints finalised their 16-player practice squad.

As Smyth retains his international player pathway [IPP] status, he can be added as a 17th member and the Saints have decided to take up that option, ensuring he will remain in New Orleans for a third season since graduating from the IPP.

articles.title: Broncos' Jonathon Cooper Pleads Not Guilty in Domestic Violence Case and Trial Is Set for November
articles.summary: ENGLEWOOD, Colo. (AP) — Denver Broncos linebacker Jonathon Cooper pleaded not guilty Monday in a Douglas County courtroom to multiple charges stemming from altercations with his then-girlfriend in June. A jury trial has been scheduled to begin on Nov. 10.
articles.body:
ENGLEWOOD, Colo. (AP) — Denver Broncos linebacker Jonathon Cooper pleaded not guilty Monday in a Douglas County courtroom to multiple charges stemming from altercations with his then-girlfriend in June. A jury trial has been scheduled to begin on Nov. 10.

Cooper was placed on the commissioner's exempt list Sunday, meaning he'll continue to get paid for the time being and will be allowed inside the team's training facility but cannot practice with the team or play in any games.

"It's part of the process," general manager George Paton said in a conference call Sunday night after the team's 53-man roster was set. "We continue to take this very seriously. We're going to continue to monitor all the legal developments and continue to support Jonathon. Jonathon's worked very hard to better himself and it'll be good to have him in the building, be in meetings and just be a part of the team."

Why was NFL star killed? New insights in 2026 documentary

Cooper pleaded not guilty to a felony charge of second-degree assault by strangulation and three misdemeanors, including violating a protection order a week after his first arrest on June 4. The strangulation charge stemmed from his first arrest after a forensic nurse examined Cooper's then-girlfriend.

Cooper was allowed to participate in training camp and on Friday was one of the Broncos' captains in their preseason finale, a 34-6 win over the Minnesota Vikings.

The league is investigating Cooper's situation and the sixth-year pro could face a lengthy suspension under the NFL's domestic violence policy. Any games he misses while on the exempt list would count toward his suspension, but he would also have to repay the money he earned while on the exempt list

"We wait on the league," coach Sean Payton said after practice Monday. "The difference now is he's in the facility, he's lifting, he's in the meetings; he can't practice. And then we just wait for this process to play out."

Cooper, who has started 52 consecutive games for the Broncos, is a key member of a defense that has led the league in sacks each of the past two seasons. He was told to stay away from the Broncos' mandatory minicamp in June following his second arrest in the span of a week.

The Broncos decided not to release Cooper, who's due $12 million this season. He was allowed to participate in training camp after attending an inpatient clinic near Vail for more than a month.

Jonah Elliss, Que Robinson and Dondrea Tillman are set to expand their workload in Cooper's absence.

"I think those guys all bring different skill sets and traits of why they're all good," said right tackle Mike McGlinchey, who squared off against all three during training camp. "Each guy brings something a little bit different in how they rush, how they set the edge, but all of them are very successful at doing it and they're going to do a great job when they get plugged in there."

articles.title: Jeremiyah Love Injury Updated Provided by Cardinals HC, Latest on RB's Status for Week 1
articles.summary: Jeremiyah Love's status for Week 1 is still up in the air.
articles.body:
Jeremiyah Love's status for Week 1 is still up in the air.

Arizona Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur was noncommittal when asked about the running back's availability for the season opener amid an ankle injury.

"Confident that he's progressing really well," LaFleur said. "He's taken another step. Took another step yesterday. He'll take another step today."

Love suffered a high ankle sprain earlier this month and was forced to miss the final two preseason games. He was solid in his sole preseason contest, rushing for 57 yards on 11 attempts against the Las Vegas Raiders.

The good news is that Love's injury didn't need surgery , which would have been a major setback to start his rookie season.

The Cardinals drafted Love third overall in April, making him the highest-drafted running back since Saquon Barkley was taken second overall by the New York Giants in 2018.

It wasn't much of a surprise to see Love taken so early. In his final season at Notre Dame, he rushed for 1,372 yards and 18 touchdowns, adding 280 yards and three touchdowns through the air.

Arizona is looking to Love to provide a spark in the backfield, but the first order of business is getting him healthy.

If Love isn't ready to go for next Sunday's game against the Los Angeles Chargers, the majority of the touches will presumably go to Tyler Allgeier, who rushed for 514 yards and eight touchdowns with the Atlanta Falcons last year.

The Cardinals had one of the worst rushing attacks in the NFL last year, mustering just 93.1 yards per game, the second-worst mark in the league. A standout year from Love wouldn't solve all of their issues, but it would address a major point of emphasis as the team continues its rebuild.

articles.title: George Kittle, Nick Bosa Injury Updates Provided by 49ers' Shanahan, Latest on Status for Week 1
articles.summary: All indications are the San Francisco 49ers will have two of their biggest superstars available for their season opener against the Los Angeles Rams.
articles.body:
All indications are the San Francisco 49ers will have two of their biggest superstars available for their season opener against the Los Angeles Rams.

Head coach Kyle Shanahan told reporters Monday that defensive end Nick Bosa and tight end George Kittle will practice this week and play in the Sept. 10 game in Australia if everything goes according to plan.

Kittle being available is not surprising.

After all, ESPN's Adam Schefter reported Sunday the tight end planned on practicing this week and "has a legitimate chance to play the opener" as he recovers from the torn Achilles he suffered in a playoff win over the Philadelphia Eagles.

San Francisco also activated Kittle from the active/physically unable to perform list last Sunday.

Returning from a torn Achilles in approximately eight months is impressive, and Schefter previously reported Kittle's recovery was "ahead of schedule."

When healthy, he is one of the best tight ends in the league with a resume that includes two First-Team All-Pro selections, four seasons with more than 1,000 receiving yards and seven Pro Bowl nods.

As for Bosa, he is recovering from a torn ACL that limited him to three games last season. Shanahan told reporters last week the pass-rusher was "doing good" and planning to practice during the upcoming week.

The latest update suggests nothing has changed from those plans.

Bosa's list of accomplishments includes a Defensive Player of the Year, Defensive Rookie of the Year, a First-Team All-Pro selection, five Pro Bowl nods and five seasons with at least nine sacks, including when he led the league with 18.5 in 2022.

His presence elevates the defense in a number of ways beyond his own sacks, as he opens up others along the line because of the double teams he draws and gets to quarterbacks quick enough that the secondary doesn't have to cover as long.

The season opener is an important one for the 49ers considering they are facing a division rival and presumed Super Bowl contender in the Rams, so having two of their best players available would be a welcome development.

articles.title: Tips for your fantasy football draft: How to build a winning team without overthinking it
articles.summary: Fantasy football draft strategy goes beyond player rankings. League scoring rules, PPR settings, roster construction, and ADP all shape your picks.
articles.body: It's that time of year again. You've read the rankings, listened to the podcasts, watched some preseason football and probably done at least one mock draft that completely fell apart by the fifth round (or you literally stopped paying attention after round three). You've got a strategy, and you're ready for your actual fantasy football draft. So, naturally, the guy in your league who hasn't done a second of research and shows up 10 minutes late asking, "Wait, Mike Evans is on the 49ers now?" is probably going to win the championship. That's fantasy football. There are hundreds, probably thousands, of fantasy football analysts on the internet, and many of them are very good at what they do. They'll tell you which running backs are undervalued, which rookie wide receivers are about to break out and which quarterback is being drafted three rounds too early. TIME TO FACE FACTS: FANTASY FOOTBALL PUNISHMENTS HAVE OFFICIALLY JUMPED THE SHARK IN 2026 Find an analyst whose opinion you trust. Better yet, find a few. That's not what we're doing here. Instead, I want to talk about general fantasy football draft strategy. I've been playing fantasy football for a long time, in a lot of different leagues with a lot of different people, and there are certain mistakes that people make over and over again. Avoiding a few of them won't guarantee you a championship. Nothing will. But it certainly won't hurt. Know the rules of your fantasy football league Let's start with the most obvious one, because it's also one that people routinely screw up: know the rules. Sounds simple, right? Well, is your league full PPR, half-PPR or standard scoring? How many wide receivers start? How many flex spots are there? Is it a one-quarterback league or superflex? Are passing touchdowns worth four points or six? Do you get bonuses for long touchdowns or 100-yard games? How many bench spots does everyone have? How does the waiver/free agency system work after the draft? All of that matters. A player can have significantly more value in one scoring system than another. A league that starts three wide receivers and a flex puts a lot more pressure on wide receiver depth than one that starts two receivers. Superflex leagues push quarterbacks way up the board. So before you start obsessing over whether Player A should be ranked 37th or 41st, make sure you understand the game you're actually playing. And that includes roster rules. I've seen people get halfway through a draft before realizing the league adjusted the roster spots between seasons. I've seen people draft like they're playing standard scoring when receptions are worth a full point. Don't be that person. This is especially important if you're playing in multiple leagues. If the setup is different enough, an elite draft in one league might be a last-place roster in another. Honestly, just knowing the rules probably puts you ahead of at least one player in your league (but likely more than one). Who are your opponents? This is one of the most important parts of fantasy football drafting, and I don't think people talk about it nearly enough. Who are you playing against? There's a huge difference between a casual home league and a league filled with people who spend all summer studying fantasy football. Maybe you're in a league with 11 friends you've known since college. Three of them are really into fantasy football. Five pay attention once the calendar flips to September but not one day sooner. One guy still thinks it's 2022. Then there's Derek, who forgot the draft was today. Side note: definitely don't be this guy. There's nothing worse than those frantic phone calls to first locate "Derek" and then, if unsuccessful, calls to find a last-minute fill-in. Home leagues are a completely different environment from a competitive league where nearly everyone understands Average Draft Position (ADP), knows the depth charts and has already done 50 drafts. If that's your league, I'm not sure why you're reading my fantasy football advice in the first place. In a casual league, good players tend to fall further. There's often no reason to reach aggressively for someone just because you like him. There's a decent chance your league mates aren't even looking at the same players you are. Sharper leagues are different. Sleepers aren't really sleepers when everyone knows about them. A player you think is going to last another round might have six other people waiting to draft him. You also need to know the specific people in your league. Home leagues develop personalities over time. One guy always takes a quarterback early. Another drafts rookies like he's waiting for his shot to be an actual NFL GM (it's not going to happen, Kevin). Someone else has to get at least three players from his favorite team every year. Pay attention. NFL COACHES AND EXECUTIVES SAY PATRICK MAHOMES IS NO LONGER THE BEST QUARTERBACK IN THE NFL I live in Connecticut, and I've made this same point about NCAA Tournament pools. Filling out a bracket against a bunch of UConn fans is different because you already know UConn is probably going to be more popular in that pool than it would be nationally. Fantasy football works the same way. Drafting with a room full of Eagles fans? Philadelphia players probably aren't slipping very far. And after 10 or 15 years in the same home league, you probably know your friends' bad habits better than they do. In fact, they probably don't even realize their own bad habits. Now is the time to use that information against them. Know where your fantasy football draft is being held Are you drafting on ESPN? Yahoo? Sleeper? CBS? NFL? Or are you sitting in someone's garage with a giant draft board and a stack of stickers? Those are not the same drafts. Every fantasy platform has its own rankings and its own ADP. And whether people realize it or not, those rankings sitting on the screen have a huge influence on who gets drafted when. A player ranked near the top of the available list is going to attract attention. Maybe you're using rankings from an analyst who has a certain wide receiver ranked 45th overall. Great. But your league is drafting on a site where that player typically goes around No. 70. Why take him at 45? You might be right about the player. But the entire point is to get him as late as you reasonably can. That's why you need to check the site you're actually using. A player you have to grab in the sixth round on ESPN might still be sitting there in the eighth on Yahoo. And that's before you even get to live drafts. There isn't one universal list controlling the room when you're sitting around a table. One person has a printout from ESPN. Another has rankings from some fantasy analyst he follows. Someone is drafting off his phone. Then there's the guy who bought a fantasy magazine in an airport six weeks ago (this guy usually falls into the "Mike Evans plays for who?!" category). Good luck figuring out what he's going to do. Those drafts can get weird quickly, which is part of what makes them fun. Rankings and ADP aren't the same thing This ties directly into the previous point. Rankings are your opinion, or somebody else's opinion, of how players should be valued. ADP tells you where people are actually taking them. You need to know both because that's how you're going to find value. Let's say you absolutely love a player and have him ranked 50th overall. His ADP is around 80. You have pick No. 52. Taking him there isn't necessarily wrong if you believe he's worth the pick. But what if you also select again at No. 69 (nice) and there's a very good chance he's still going to be available? Now you've got a decision to make. Fantasy football isn't just about identifying good players. It's also about figuring out how long you can afford to wait before somebody else takes them. Of course, ADP isn't some magical law that everyone has to follow. Players get picked ahead of ADP all the time, and sometimes that's the right move. Same thing with rankings. There isn't nearly enough certainty in fantasy football to pretend that the player ranked 42nd is definitely better than the player ranked 49th. They're probably pretty close. That's why tiers can be useful. You might have six wide receivers that you view almost identically who are all still available. Meanwhile, there's one running back left before you see a significant drop at the position. That matters a lot more than whether WR18 is technically ranked three spots ahead of RB17. Don't panic because everyone else is drafting one position It happens in almost every fantasy draft. Three quarterbacks go in quick succession. Then someone takes another one. Suddenly, a person who had absolutely no intention of drafting a quarterback starts thinking, "Oh no, I need to get one." Do you? Maybe. But it's also possible four people just helped you by taking quarterbacks while good players at other positions sat there. Obviously, you can't completely ignore a run. If the last quarterback you really like is sitting there and six have already gone, you might have to pull the trigger. But that's different from getting nervous because the room suddenly decided now is the time to grab QB1. There are drafts where jumping into the run makes sense. There are others where I'm perfectly happy watching everyone else do it and taking whatever good players they're leaving for me. This is called "board texture" if you're really into fantasy football, and I promise that's the last time I'm going to use a nerdy term like that. You're building a fantasy roster, not completing a checklist There's something satisfying about looking at your fantasy team during the draft and seeing every starting position filled. Quarterback? Got one. Running backs? Done. Wide receivers? Check. Tight end? Taken care of. Defense and kicker? Yep, got them, too. Great. Nobody gives you bonus points for that. Your goal isn't to be the first person in the league with a complete Week 1 starting lineup. You're trying to build a roster for an entire season. Maybe there's a tight end you like, but there are four others you'd be perfectly happy drafting later. Meanwhile, a running back you had ranked much higher than the rest of the board is still available even though you already have two running backs. I'm probably taking RB3 and dealing with tight end later. Obviously, this has limits. You can't completely ignore roster construction and just draft 14 running backs because they're the highest-ranked player every time you're on the clock. But I see people pass on good players all the time because they don't like seeing an empty spot next to "TE" or "QB" on the draft screen. Don't turn every sleeper into a reach Everyone loves sleepers. It's one of the best parts of fantasy football, and if you Google "fantasy football sleepers" you'll probably get 10,000 results. Why? Every analyst writes those articles because they know how many people are looking for that exact analysis. There's no better feeling than taking the guy no one in your league has even heard of and having him post a 1,000-yard, 10 TD season. Now you get to talk about what a football expert you are (but you're still not getting that GM gig, Kevin). The problem is that fantasy players sometimes get so excited about finding sleepers that they destroy the entire point of finding them. A player isn't much of a bargain if you draft him four rounds ahead of where anyone else was going to take him. Now, there's nothing wrong with reaching sometimes. In fact, you have to do it. Fantasy drafts don't let you select whenever you want. Maybe you pick 65th and don't pick again until 88th. There's a player with an ADP around 78 whom you really want. Take him. Waiting around for some perfect ADP value is a good way to watch the guy picking three spots behind you draft all the players you wanted. But taking someone 15 picks early because you know he won't make it back to you is different from taking someone 50 picks early because you watched two preseason highlights and fell in love. And, yes, maybe you really did find the next superstar. I'd still rather draft him later if I can. Be ready for your fantasy football draft to go completely sideways You can do 100 mock drafts before your real draft (but you shouldn't, because this is a major waste of time). It won't matter. Someone is going to take a player 25 picks earlier than expected. A player you've never seen fall past the fifth round is going to be sitting there in the seventh. You're going to have three players queued up for your next pick and watch all three come off the board right before you're on the clock. Welcome to fantasy football. This is why I never go into a draft thinking things like, "I'm definitely taking two running backs with my first two picks." Maybe that's how it works out. Then again, maybe the second round comes around and a receiver you never expected to see is sitting there. Same with waiting for a quarterback, taking an elite tight end early or any other draft strategy you decided on before the first team was even on the clock. Having a plan is smart. Just don't spend the entire draft trying to force the board to match the mock draft you did Tuesday night. Most importantly, fantasy football is supposed to be fun I saved this one for last because I think people sometimes forget it. Fantasy football is supposed to be fun. Yes, we all want to win. Winning is a lot more fun than losing. And everything written above is designed to help you make better decisions during your draft. But you're also going to spend the next four months rooting for these players. You'll watch a random Monday Night Football game between two teams you don't care about because you need 11 points from your wide receiver (I'm looking at you, Falcons at Saints in Week 4). You'll spend Sunday afternoon checking your phone to see whether your running back got credit for a reception (c'mon, that wasn't a lateral; he definitely threw it forward!) You're going to care about these guys. So, if there's a player you really like, and you want him on your fantasy team, take him. Maybe it's your favorite player. Maybe you just really want to root for the guy this season. That's good enough for me. Take him. Does that mean you should take someone with a 10th-round ADP in the third round because you really like him? Probably not. But we're talking about fantasy football here, not managing your 401(k) (unless you're in a league where you're playing for the value of someone's 401(k), but again, you're probably not taking advice from me if that's the case). CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP So pick a player a little earlier than ADP if you really want him. Who cares if some fantasy expert has another guy ranked two spots higher? Do your homework. Understand the room you're drafting in and try not to light value on fire for no reason. After that, get some players you actually like. You might even win the league. If you do, don't forget to tell everyone how good you are at fantasy football. And if you don't, blame injuries and bad luck. That's what everyone else does.

articles.title: Kansas City Chiefs may have ruined Jack Pyburn's plan to make big money at LSU  by giving him a job in the NFL
articles.summary: Jack Pyburn was set to earn more at LSU than his NFL rookie salary, but the Kansas City Chiefs claimed the linebacker off waivers from Tampa Bay.
articles.body: Folks who track such things last week were estimating that Jack Pyburn could make around $1 million in 2026 if he was cut by the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and allowed to return to college at LSU. Except, well, the Kansas City Chiefs had other plans. The Chiefs on Monday afternoon claimed the linebacker off waivers from the Bucs, per the NFL waiver wire. That means Pyburn's NFL career continues as a member of the Chiefs' 53-man roster. NCAA CREATED THIS MESS, NOW LSU SET TO MAKE DAE’QUAN WRIGHT COLLEGE FOOTBALL’S FIRST NFL RETURNEE It also means Pyburn is seemingly headed for a pay cut by being in the NFL rather than back in college. Yes, crazy world. Pyburn's rookie salary is scheduled to be $885,000. And that is less than the $1 million he was expected to make in college. So we have reached the critical juncture where the NIL rules and countless court filings and rulings on eligibility have turned college football into something of a financial competitor for the NFL in the case of some players. MATT RHULE SOUNDS ALARM ON NFL RETURNEES, $45 MILLION ROSTERS AND COLLEGE FOOTBALL’S PAYROLL PROBLEM It's been that way before. There have been examples where quarterbacks forego their final years in college and the sizeable pay they might have earned in that season, and go to the NFL to take a financial shave. But that's quarterbacks. Stars. And it is their choice to start what promises to be a lucrative career longterm. Jack Pyburn? He was not drafted in April coming out of LSU. He played only one season there after playing at the University of Florida in 2023 and 2024. Pyburn played in 12 games with 11 starts at LSU and collected 52 tackles with 2 sacks and 5.5 tackles for loss. That's nice. But that doesn't scream $1 million nice. NCAA WINS TENTH CIRCUIT 'STAY', BUT FACES MORE ELIGIBILITY LAWSUITS FROM 2022 CLASS ATHLETES IN CHAOTIC TIME And how did we get here? Pyburn was part of a lawsuit filed by more than 30 athletes in Louisiana that won a temporary restraining order allowing them to play in college in the 2026 academic year. Pyburn and other players meeting certain criteria who signed with or were drafted by NFL teams were allowed to return to school as long as they could terminate their pro contracts and repay any pro earnings. Pyburn was reportedly ready to do that with the Bucs because they were expected to cut him – as they eventually did. They had guaranteed him $115,000, including a $15,000 signing bonus. CLICK HERE TO GET THE FOX NEWS APP But now that contract is not terminated. It and the rights to Pyburn belong to the Chiefs. Pyburn, by the way, reportedly informed LSU that he is withdrawing his name from the ongoing eligibility lawsuit and will remain in the NFL – not that the Chiefs gave him a choice, really. articles.title: Matthew Berry details how he reported Tom Brady signing with Tampa Bay while drunk at a bar with team official
articles.summary: Matthew Berry revealed to OutKick how a late-night bar encounter at the NFL Combine led him to first report Tom Brady's move to Tampa Bay.
articles.body: Do you remember who first reported that Tom Brady would join the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in 2020? Matthew Berry thought about the question for a brief moment before remembering. "Oh, I believe it was me," he told OutKick. For context, Brady announced his departure from the New England Patriots weeks before signing with Tampa Bay. At the time, his rumored destinations included the Los Angeles Chargers, Las Vegas Raiders and Indianapolis Colts. No one had mentioned the Buccaneers. MATTHEW BERRY DISCUSSES WHETHER HE'D HIRE DIANNA RUSSINI FOR HIS BUDDING FANTASY FOOTBALL EMPIRE Then, after the NFL Combine, Berry wrote in his annual rumors column that he would bet on Brady heading to Tampa. He told OutKick he was quite confident about his prediction at the time. "I won’t give away my source, but I will tell you how I came across the information. I was at the NFL Combine, and it was about 2 a.m., and I was in a bar. I met somebody who worked for the Buccaneers organization," he explained. "We were drinking for an hour and were hammered. This particular person tells me, ‘I think we have a shot at Brady.’ And I’m like, ‘No, you don’t.’" Berry added: "And this person tells me, ‘No, man. We worked him out. We’ve had conversations with him. We think it’s down to us and, I think he said, the Raiders. He goes, Gisele wants a South Florida team to make it easier for her to get home, to fly out of a Florida airport." As they continued drinking, Berry realized the person was, in fact, serious. "The more he talked, the more convinced this person sounded. I thought, ‘Well, okay.’ These are things that I hear drunk in a bar." MATTHEW BERRY HAS HAD TALKS WITH ESPN ABOUT A RETURN, FOLLOWING PAT MCAFEE MODEL As I mentioned to Berry during the conversation, I remember reading his report and asking an NFL insider about it. The insider said they had not heard that. Fans and media were also skeptical that a fantasy football guru, rather than a traditional insider, would have the correct information about one of the biggest transactions in NFL history. Later that night, the insider texted me back: "Berry is onto something." Brady eventually signed with Tampa Bay and led the Buccaneers to a Super Bowl victory in his first season there. The takeaway is obvious. For those who want to break major NFL stories, the real information is not obtained at journalism school, but while drunk in a bar at 2 a.m. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Berry appreciated that we asked him about the scoop. "No one has ever brought that up before. Thank you." You can watch OutKick's full interview with Matthew Berry on YouTube here.

articles.title: Broncos LB Jonathon Cooper pleads not guilty to all charges, 1 day after placement on commissioner's exempt list for alleged domestic violence incident
articles.summary: Cooper is now scheduled to face a trial by jury that will take place during Denver's bye week. He's been arrested twice over an alleged incident of domestic...
articles.body:
Content warning: This article contains depictions of alleged domestic violence.

Denver Broncos linebacker Jonathan Cooper pleaded not guilty on Monday to all charges related to his multiple arrests for an alleged instance of domestic violence.

Cooper entered his pleas in a Douglas County, Colorado, courtroom, one day after news broke that he'll start the NFL season on the commissioner's exempt list because of the charges.

Cooper is now slated to face a jury trial scheduled for Nov. 10, 12 and 13. The trial will take place during Denver's bye week.

Cooper's placement on the commissioner's exempt list means that he won't be permitted to practice or play as long as he's on it. Cooper will be permitted to attend team meetings. He won't count against Denver's 53-man roster that was set by the NFL's roster cut-down deadline Sunday afternoon.

How long Cooper remains on this list is unclear. The commissioner's exempt list is managed at the discretion of NFL commissioner Roger Goodell.

Cooper allegedly strangled his then-girlfriend

Cooper was arrested twice in the same week in June in relation to an alleged domestic violence incident involving his girlfriend. Per court records cited by local reports in Denver, Cooper and his long-term girlfriend were both arrested on June 4 and each charged with criminal mischief as a crime of domestic violence. The charge against Cooper's girlfriend was later dropped.

Per police records, the alleged incident took place during an argument in which Cooper's girlfriend accused him of cheating on her. Per those records, Cooper's girlfriend said she threw his phone across the room, then went to retrieve it to look through it.

Cooper told police that he grabbed his girlfriend by her upper arm and took the phone back and "braced his neck against her neck" in the process. He said he threatened to break her phone if she didn't leave his apartment; police affidavits show that he did bite her phone when she didn't leave.

Cooper's girlfriend told a different story that he "grabbed her by the neck" and held her up against the wall. She also said Cooper picked her up and threw her back on the ground several times and punched the wall "next to her face," according to the police report.

Officers on the scene noted in their report that her injuries "did not appear consistent with a larger male lifting [her] up into the air by her throat as well as repeatedly being thrown to the ground."

Medical exam led to felony assault charge

Cooper pleaded not guilty to the initial charges in court the next week. He was placed under a protection order that he was not to "harass, molest, intimidate, retaliate against or tamper" with his girlfriend. Prosecutors say that Cooper violated that order by sending her multiple text messages and going to her home.

Police arrested Cooper again on June 11 on four new charges, per Denver's 9 News :

Felony second-degree assault — strangulation

Third-degree assault — knowingly or recklessly causing injury

Prosecutors added the felony assault charge after a medical examination stated that Cooper's girlfriend suffered "serious bodily injury" in the incident. A nurse's report obtained by police described her injuries as consistent with "strangulation with hypoxia."

Cooper faced his arraignment and pleaded not guilty Monday, and he'll face trial in November. An NFL investigation remains ongoing. It's not clear when or if he'll be cleared to play for the Broncos.

The Broncos excused Cooper from mandatory minicamp upon his second arrest. He returned to the team and was a full participant with Denver's starters in training camp and suited up for all three of Denver's preseason games. The Broncos named Cooper a captain for Friday's preseason finale against the Minnesota Vikings.

Cooper, a five-year NFL veteran and seventh-round pick in the 2021 NFL Draft, has emerged as a full-time starter for the Broncos. He started in all of Denver's 17 regular-season games in each of the previous three seasons.

Cooper has recorded eight-plus sacks in each of the past three seasons, including a career-high 10.5 in 2024. He has 31.5 sacks for his career and is considered a key contributor to a Broncos defense that projects as one of the best in the NFL.

Head coach Sean Payton addressed Cooper's situation with reporters on July 29 at the onset of training camp.

"We're staying course with league protocol, club protocol, relative to what we're advised to do," Payton said. "He's been fantastic working away from the building, and we'll continue to do that and monitor it.

"We're supportive, and yet, very much aware of the seriousness of these type of things. … We're proud of the work he did these last, we'll call it a month and a half. It wasn't easy. It will continue to be a challenge. We'll see where it goes. But fully supportive of him right now as we gather all the information, and we'll go from there."

articles.title: Odell Beckham Jr. Reacts to Making Giants Roster in Emotional Video, Hints at Number Change
articles.summary: Making the roster for the New York Giants is a full-circle moment for Odell Beckham Jr.
articles.body:
Making the roster for the New York Giants is a full-circle moment for Odell Beckham Jr.

"I had tears when I got back to the hotel and realized I was going to be here," he told reporters Monday after remaining on the team past Sunday's roster cut deadline. He also said he "definitely had that moment where it was like, you could let out some of the pain that I feel like I went through."

What's more, the wide receiver revealed he will have "conversations" about potentially being No. 13:

Whether Beckham would make the roster was one of the more notable storylines of training camp and the preseason for the Giants.

After all, there was a time when he was one of the best players in the organization after New York selected him with the No. 12 overall pick of the 2014 NFL draft. He was the Offensive Rookie of the Year in his first season and made the Pro Bowl in each of his first three.

He surpassed 1,300 receiving yards in each of those three seasons as well.

Beckham has since bounced around to the Cleveland Browns, Los Angeles Rams, Baltimore Ravens and Miami Dolphins and most notably helped lead the Rams to a Super Bowl title during the 2021 campaign.

However, he also suffered a torn ACL during that Super Bowl win, missed the 2022 season and played just nine games in 2024. He didn't play in 2025, although he made it clear he wasn't retiring .

There will be no retirement ahead of the 2026 season, as the 33-year-old made the roster of the team he is most closely associated with from earlier in his career.

With Malik Nabers, Darnell Mooney and Malachi Fields also on the roster, Beckham won't be the primary focal point of the aerial attack like he was during his first stint with the Giants. But that also means he could face more favorable matchups with opposing defenses focused on the other options.

And that could lead to a solid season for the veteran.

articles.title: Rickey Jackson wins first Bassmaster Randy Moss Pro Football Hall of Fame Pro-Am on St. Lawrence River
articles.summary: Rickey Jackson edged Joe Thomas by just 5 ounces to win the first Bassmaster Randy Moss Pro-Am on the St. Lawrence River in Clayton, New York.
articles.body: CLAYTON, NEW YORK — The first-ever Bassmaster Randy Moss Pro Football Hall of Fame Pro-Am wrapped Monday on the St. Lawrence River in Clayton, New York. And, surprisingly enough, it wasn’t Randy Moss who took home the trophy. The event paired eight Hall of Famers with eight Bassmaster Elite pros for a single day on the water. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK OUTDOORS Here's how the football side of the field stacked up. The champion: Rickey Jackson Super Bowl XXIX champion linebacker Rickey Jackson, paired with two-time Bassmaster Classic qualifier John Garrett, won the whole thing with 21 pounds, 10 ounces. Jackson, a Pahokee, Fla., native who grew up around Lake Okeechobee, compared the win to the biggest stage he knows: "I mean, it's kind of like winning the Super Bowl." DENNY HAMLIN CHASES MONSTER LARGEMOUTH BASS IN TEXAS WITH BASSMASTER PRO CHRIS ZALDAIN Minus the free trip to Disney World, of course. Runner-up: Joe Thomas backed up the big talk Joe Thomas spent tournament week loudly promising a win and needling Randy Moss over the tournament bearing his name. "I would say these guys are trembling in their boots because I am by far the most experienced and talented of the bass fishermen here, pros included," Thomas (jokingly, we think) told OutKick Outdoors on the dock just before launch. "I mean, it's just a matter of when we collect our prize money and the trophy at this point. He and his partner, Jay Przekurat, nearly made good on the promise, too, finishing second at 21-5, just 5 ounces short of the win. Thomas kept the trash talk going all the way to the scale: "It would feel great to snatch that right from Randy Moss because he's been cheating a little bit... but as you can see, when you're from Wisconsin, you guys can cheat all you want, Randy Moss. The real fishermen are right here. We'll take care of it." Third place: Kevin Mawae needs a boat Offensive lineman Kevin Mawae finished third at 20-6 alongside Robert Gee. Mawae turned out to be no stranger to the sport, revealing he lives near Toledo Bend Reservoir. It’s one of the top bass fisheries in the country, and he spends plenty of time there. EVAN KUNG WINS BASSMASTER ELITE AT ST. LAWRENCE RIVER IN A TOURNAMENT FOR THE RECORD BOOKS Asked if he was ready to join the pro tour, Mawae explained that he still needed three things: his wife’s blessing, sponsors and a boat. "You don't have to have a boat," he said. "But you gotta make sure you're friendly with a neighbor who does." Words of wisdom from the Hall of Famer there. Fourth place: Dave Robinson's beef jerky gambit Packers legend Dave Robinson, who won the first two Super Bowls under Vince Lombardi, finished fourth at 17-15 with 2024 Bassmaster Classic champion Justin Hamner. Robinson came into the week with tremendously low expectations for himself. When we asked him to rate his confidence ahead of the tournament, Robinson gave his own fishing skills a "negative two" out of 10. But he still predicted a win. On the water, Hamner revealed Robinson tried a creative approach to baiting his hook: "He had beef jerky on the hook. I don't know if that's cheating or not, but I just wanted to let y'all know." It didn't work — no fish were caught on the jerky — but it was worth a shot. Fifth place: Ronde Barber is still thinking about football Cornerback Ronde Barber and Elite pro Tucker Smith finished fifth at 16-14. When asked what position his partner could play in the NFL, Barber tasked him to cover Randy Moss. "He's going to play Nickelback next to me," Barber said. "He’s going to be my backup." Way, way, way back, B.A.S.S. emcee Dave Mercer noted. Sixth place: Robert Brazile, aka "Doctor Doom" Robert Brazile, competing under his old NFL nickname "Doctor Doom" alongside partner Tyler Williams, finished sixth at 14-3. Together, they were "Doctor Doom and the Barefoot Bandit." If there’s ever been a better name for a fishing duo, we’ve certainly never heard it. Brazile leaned into his father's old fishing wisdom, explaining, "The best way to fish is to close your mouth." Which really just sounds like his dad wanted some peace and quiet on the water. Still, the advice stuck. "I never thought I could enjoy something more than football," Brazile concluded. "This is better than football." The man behind the event: Randy Moss Fishing with 2025 Bassmaster Classic champion Easton Fothergill, Moss weighed in at 13-11, good for seventh place. Fothergill, who grew up in Minnesota idolizing Moss, said his partner held his own on the water, using forward-facing sonar to locate fish sitting 70 to 90 feet deep. Moss put this event together specifically to give his Hall of Fame brothers an experience he fell in love with roughly two decades ago. "I just wanted to team up, bring the two together, and see if we can put something on for years to come," Moss told OutKick Outdoors before the tournament. "This is the first annual, and I look forward to it." He described the event as a way to pull his fellow Hall of Famers out of the football-only orbit they usually share once a year at induction, and into something new. And the beauty of the St. Lawrence River in Clayton was an easy selling point. "Me being a country boy," Moss said, "just being around water just makes me feel at home." Eighth place, but not empty-handed: Calvin Johnson Megatron and Elite pro Brandon Palaniuk finished last as a team at 11-13 — but still walked away with the day's Phoenix Boats Big Bass award anyway, boating a 7-pound smallmouth. Johnson, ever humble about it, downplayed his own role. "I was just fishing today. I wasn't catching." It happens like that sometimes. But he did admit the day left an impression. "This is truly a one-of-a-kind experience for me," Johnson said. "I was talking to Brandon, I was like, 'Dang man, you got me thinking about getting a boat now.'" If Monday was any indication, Megatron won't be the only one. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Moss set out to build something his fellow Hall of Famers would fall in love with the same way he did. And based on the reactions up and down the dock, it worked. Next year, something tells me there’ll be more than just eight teams. Love all things fishing and outdoors? articles.title: Shedeur Sanders, Dillon Gabriel Trade Buzz Updated in New NFL Rumors After Browns Set 53-Man Roster
articles.summary: The Cleveland Browns set their 53-man roster on Sunday, and to the surprise of many, they kept all four of their quarterbacks.
articles.body:
The Cleveland Browns set their 53-man roster on Sunday, and to the surprise of many, they kept all four of their quarterbacks.

But there's a world in which Dillon Gabriel or Shedeur Sanders isn't with the team by the end of the season.

According to Fox Sports' Eric Williams , one scout said the Browns could be keeping Gabriel around in hopes of trading him for draft compensation, as they did with Joe Flacco and Kenny Pickett in 2025.

Another scenario could see Gabriel take over the No. 2 spot, with Sanders hitting the trade block.

"It will be interesting how it unfolds," the NFL scout told Williams. "From the outside, you'd want to go with experience and leadership at QB over everything else at this point. But I think Gabriel has a chance to be a good backup and liked him coming out.

"All eyes are on Sanders, but he's gotta show he can be a solid, strong leader and settle down as well to grind, learn and develop. He's going to find out that as a player, you can only get so many opportunities to do that, and you better take advantage of every single one of them."

Gabriel appeared in 10 games for the Browns last year and threw for 937 yards, seven touchdowns and two interceptions. When he suffered a concussion in November, Sanders replaced him and eventually closed out the season as the starter.

Sanders finished the 2025 campaign with 1,400 yards, seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions in eight games.

Sanders spent the offseason competing with Deshaun Watson for the starting job before eventually losing the battle to the veteran. Gabriel's performance in the final preseason game perhaps boosted his status, though, as he threw for 186 yards and three touchdowns on 12-of-15 passing.

Whatever direction the Browns decide to take with their quarterback room could take a while to materialize, though, since Gabriel is starting the year on the injured reserve after suffering a back injury.

articles.title: Brandon Aiyuk $24.9M Contract Bonus Addressed by 49ers' John Lynch Amid WR's Reserved List Stint
articles.summary: Veteran receiver Brandon Aiyuk is due a $24.9 million option bonus from the San Francisco 49ers if he's on the roster Sept. 1, though because he remains on the reserve/left squad list, the Niners don't currently owe him that payout.
articles.body:
Veteran receiver Brandon Aiyuk is due a $24.9 million option bonus from the San Francisco 49ers if he's on the roster Sept. 1, though because he remains on the reserve/left squad list, the Niners don't currently owe him that payout.

"Nothing changed there," general manager John Lynch told reporters Monday. "He's on the reserve/left squad list, and as such he's just kinda not on our roster."

When further asked about Aiyuk not currently getting paid anything he would otherwise be due on Sept. 1 given the current designation, he answered that was "correct."

Aiyuk has been on the reserve/left squad list since December, the culmination in a long drama with the Niners. After suffering a torn ACL and MCL in the 2024 season, he didn't participate in the team's scheduled rehab sessions and the Niners voided the guarantees in his deal.

He essentially ghosted the team from there and said in July he had no intention of requesting reinstatement with the team (which he would need to do to be removed from the reserve/left squad list).

"I will not be reinstating with them or ever doing any kind of business with them," he wrote in a social media post . "I'm locked in and focused on my opportunity to return to the field this season!"

The issue for Aiyuk is that he has no pathway to return to the field unless the Niners trade him or release him. At the moment they don't seem inclined to do either, given they don't currently owe him any money. If Aiyuk wants to play in the 2026 season, he'll first need to reinstate with the team, at which point they would assuredly release him.

But if Aiyuk waits until after the Nov. 10 trade deadline to do so, the Niners could outright deny any request for reinstatement. So for this situation to end, Aiyuk needs to act sooner rather than later.

articles.title: How did Ravens coach Jesse Minter end up rapping Eminem for the team? Inside Baltimore’s culture shift, where young play-callers are more than just young
articles.summary: After 18 years with John Harbaugh as the Ravens head coach, a new and needed energy shift has arrived. That’s by design. It’s not a knock on Harbaugh, but so...
articles.body:
OWINGS MILLS, Md. — Jesse Minter's performance went viral.

But at the Baltimore Ravens' team dinner, he was not the first coach to take the mic. And staff performances were not part of the plan.

The Ravens' dinner, scheduled during their trip to Minnesota for joint practices and a preseason game against the Vikings, featured a standard NFL tradition: rookie players singing before the rest of the team.

Second-round rookie edge rusher Zion Young asked defensive coordinator Anthony Weaver if he could perform another act. Young had already shown his defensive teammates his imitation of Weaver; could Young show his Weaver bit to the whole team?

Weaver agreed, but cautioned Young: Your defensive teammates have already seen this and your offensive teammates won't catch many of your references. Young risked the flop.

"So it was a dud, it was bad," Weaver told Yahoo Sports of the imitation he admitted was "hilarious" the first time around. "I did warn him. I did. I tried to. That's my job as a coach: Try and save you. So I got up there and sang to save him from the ridicule from his teammates.

"I essentially got up there and changed the focus of attention."

As Weaver's rendition of Anthony Hamilton's "Charlene" impressed players, an energetic room continued to call for coaches.

"Double D!" wide receiver Zay Flowers exclaimed into the microphone afterward.

Offensive coordinator Declan Doyle hadn't expected to sing, but the detail-oriented coach considered his cues as he reached the front of the room.

"Similar to how I call plays, I was thinking about like, 'All right, what are the boys going to know?'" Doyle told Yahoo Sports. "You watch rookie performances and they're literally all about enthusiasm. And as long as you don't forget the words, and you're enthusiastic and you have energy, you should be fine."

So Doyle pulled off his rendition of "Shot for Me" by Drake. Then momentum turned toward the Ravens head coach.

Would Minter, a steady-energy personality like Doyle, let loose and sing? The question wasn't what artist he'd choose — Weaver had already correctly guessed Minter's Eminem fandom at a spring uniform reveal event for fans . But would Minter, a rookie head coach, play into a ruse he had the option to avoid?

Minter's 30+ seconds of Eminem's "Lose Yourself" energized the room and soon the internet after highly touted rookie receiver Ja'Kobi Lane shared a clip on Instagram. Players gathered around a table of half-eaten key lime pie and partially drank water glasses, singing along. The moment felt almost natural despite the surprise.

Because after 18 years with John Harbaugh as the Ravens head coach, a new and needed energy shift has arrived. That's by design. It's not a knock on Harbaugh, whose culture is now animating his New York Giants locker room. But sometimes messages lose their edge — as parents and children across time have seen — and disciples are more willing to listen to a new source.

Enter 43-year-old Minter to replace the 63-year-old Harbaugh, and 30-year-old Doyle taking over for 60-year-old Todd Monken (now the Cleveland Browns head coach). A youth movement has arrived in Baltimore. Players noticed even before Minter rapped "Lose Yourself," which he figured would resonate despite its 2002 release given Eminem had "survived the last 10 years on my playlist." And they're well aware after it.

"For him to end it off like that kind of shows that at the end of the day, he's our leader, but at the same time, he's going through everything we're going through and he's willing to do the things that it takes," cornerback Chidobe Awuzie told Yahoo Sports. "Some coaches [would] be like, 'Oh no, I'm too big for that.' But [Minter] got up there, turned us all up, had a great time.

"You have a coach that has that energy, it just reinforces all those things that we're trying to get out of the game."

While Ravens D could look similar, Lamar Jackson and offense are changing

From the Ravens' Jan. 22 hiring of Minter to their early February hiring of Doyle, Baltimore did not simply hire young play-callers for the sake of hiring young play-callers.

Minter arrives in Baltimore after coordinating consecutive top-10 scoring defenses for the Los Angeles Chargers. Doyle earns his second straight promotion from a boss under which he's not previously worked, after coordinating Chicago Bears head coach Ben Johnson's top-10 scoring offense.

Minter and Weaver each return to Baltimore after prior stints coaching there in the last decade, creating a continuity with recent Ravens units that leaned into physicality and aggressiveness. Baltimore maintained its hold on top-10 defenses in terms of scoring and yardage from 2022-2024 before falling to 18th in points allowed and 24th in yardage last season.

With a defensive line that now features edge rusher Trey Hendrickson and Young, and a secondary that continues to be anchored by chess piece Kyle Hamilton, the Ravens' first-team defense created problems for both the Vikings and the Washington Commanders in August joint practices.

Weaver references a film review from their joint practice in Minnesota, the camera angle just behind Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray. The Ravens had dropped eight defenders in coverage on a red-zone play that presented a third-and-5 play, give or take.

"There was no place to go for the ball," Weaver said. "You just felt the pocket with Calais [Campbell] and Trey [Hendrickson] and [Tavius Robinson] out there right on three-man rush. And that's not even all rushers out.

"But when I think about that, that's what you constantly want to see. You just want to see suffocating defense."

A suffocating defense could give an offense undergoing more noticeable shifts room to breathe.

In Lamar Jackson's ninth season, expect more under-center work from the two-time MVP who has not been primarily under center since youth football, he said. Expect Jackson's throwing mechanics to shift from a right-foot-forward motion to a left-foot-forward motion that Shanahan-McVay and West Coast system teams across the league believe is imperative to the timing of the passing game.

"Everything in the dropback passing game times up with that left foot forward," Doyle said. "That took a little bit, not a little discussion, but I wanted to make sure he felt comfortable doing it before we were like, 'Hey, let's just go down that path.' He felt really good about it, and so we started working in the spring, and it's come really natural to him."

Also natural to Jackson, in Doyle's vantage point: taking coaching points.

Doyle insisted on meeting with Jackson before accepting the Ravens' job offer, 30-year-old play caller and 29-year-old quarterback Zooming for an hour in that process to get on the same page. Regular communication has continued. After a series of five plays in practice, Doyle finds Jackson to ask: "What'd you see here? What'd you see here ?" On the Ravens' first off day of training camp, Jackson and Doyle met in Doyle's office for 3 ½ hours to watch film and swap ideas from their past.

"Whatever it is, it's a pass concept, I've seen that pass concept hit so many times that I have a Rolodex of things in my head of how to teach that and coach that," Doyle said. "He's thrown it so many times that he's got a Rolodex. And so we're constantly trying to adjust and fix problems and get on the same page.

"It's just this rabbit hole that you're going down together."

This Ravens staff knows it arrives to a team with a quarterback who's won 76 of 107 career starts, completing 64.8% of his passes for 22,608 yards and 187 touchdowns to 56 interceptions. Jackson's 102.2 career passer rating leads the NFL all-time, per Pro Football Reference. That mark doesn't even factor in the dual-threat Jackson's 6,522 yards and 35 touchdowns rushing in the regular season.

What's the key to coaching a player who's already achieved so much success? Minter and Doyle are eager to scheme Jackson's rare talent arsenal in collaboration with their quarterback while remaining unafraid to coach him hard and ask him to implement new concepts. Jackson saw that firsthand during OTAs when he was supposed to run a bootleg play-action play and instead tossed the ball as if he were assigned a run play. Jackson told reporters afterward that Doyle yelled: "Lamar, what the F are you doing?" The quarterback learned that the coordinator he'd praised for creativity and "mind-blowing" detail was also not afraid to lay down the law.

"I let him know that that was not correct and he responded to that right away because at the end of the day, he's a guy that wants to be coached," Doyle said. "He's very coachable. He wants to get it right. And at the same point in time, you want to make sure that he knows, 'Hey, this is the standard and I don't care who you are.'

"If you're the starting quarterback or you're our fourth guy, you're going to be held to a certain standard."

Ravens on Minter: 'Unapologetically who he is'

Creating expectations from preseason play is a dangerous, and usually foolish, practice in the NFL. Team strategies range on whether to play or sit starters, and how much of a playbook to reveal. Discrepancies skew predictive accuracy.

The Ravens nonetheless leaned into a historical franchise interest in winning preseason games this year.

The result: No defense allowed fewer points per preseason game than the Ravens' 4.3, only the Harbaugh-coached Giants (7.3) joining Baltimore in allowing fewer than 10. And no team came within 5 points of the Ravens' league-best 21.7-point preseason game scoring differential. The Super Bowl-favorite Los Angeles Rams ranked second, beating teams by an average of 14.7 points.

"You really want to play to your identity, and you want to create a play style of how you play in all three phases," Minter told reporters. "What are your standards? What are you accepting as playing for the Ravens? And the thing I am really most proud of is that all the guys out there play the way we want to play."

Baltimore will see whether that win-every-chance mindset translates to the regular season. And the Ravens will receive some degree of cushion as they acclimate.

Because not until Week 8, at the Buffalo Bills, will Baltimore face a team that advanced to the playoffs last season. An early slate beginning with the Indianapolis Colts and New Orleans Saints should give Jackson and Co. a chance to adjust to their new offensive system, while Minter gets his feel for the new personnel against which he's calling plays. The NFL's arc toward parity means some of those missed-playoff teams could be more competitive than their 2025 season suggests, most notably the Ravens' Week 3 opponent: The Ravens will face the Dallas Cowboys in Rio de Janeiro, a long plane ride before a game against a team returning a potent offense and revamped defense.

Still, tougher on-paper games against the Bills, Jacksonville Jaguars, Los Angeles Chargers and Houston Texans won't hit until later in the season.

Players are eager to see what their schemes look like by then, from defenders wondering how Hamilton creeps from the deep backfield closer to the ball, to Baltimore's offensive cast marveling at Jackson seeming to have eyes on the sides of the head as he hits rollout targets that seem to defy the limits of human peripheral vision. All eyes will be on Jackson's health and mobility, too: When asked recently about his career low 5.2 rushing attempts per game last year (Jackson's prior seasons had ranged from 8.2-11.7), he pointed to the slew of injuries that also limited him to 11 full games last year.

And how will the coaching staff navigate the tides of an NFL season? The even-keeled nature of their play-callers encourages the roster, tight end Durham Smythe said. Smythe, who played for the Miami Dolphins and Bears before joining Baltimore, said he's often asked how he likes his head coach and coordinator.

"And I'm always like, 'If you ask me before the season, I love them, but you don't really know a person until the bullets are flying, you lose a game, you lose two games in regular season,'" Smythe told Yahoo Sports. "But I am just very confident in those guys in terms of how this team is going to react when something does go wrong, which you can't always say."

That steady demeanor made Minter and Doyle's Eminem and Drake performances that much more thrilling for players, who didn't expect the rise in energy their coaches delivered in Minnesota.

Weaver watched Minter rap lyric after lyric, noticing how players responded.

"You could just tell the guys are drawn to just his humanity and vulnerability, and the fact that he is who he is and unapologetically who he is," Weaver said. "The guys respect that."
