NFL Network's Mike Garafolo reported Monday that former Jacksonville Jaguars tight end Patrick Herbert, who is Justin's brother, is joining the Chargers' practice squad after the AFC South team waived him ahead of Sunday's roster-cut deadline.

According to Garafolo, Herbert received offers from multiple teams before deciding to join his brother on the Chargers.

The Herbert brothers played together at Oregon during the 2019 campaign and helped lead the Ducks to a 12-win season that ended with a Rose Bowl victory over Wisconsin.

Patrick Herbert does not have a catch in the regular season at the NFL level, although he tallied stats in the Jaguars' preseason victories over the New Orleans Saints and Tampa Bay Buccaneers ahead of the 2026 campaign.

He finished with two tackles against the Saints and posted two catches for 12 yards against the Buccaneers.

With Charlie Kolar, Oronde Gadsden and David Njoku all on the roster, there may not be much playing time at tight end for Herbert. But if he does get a chance, he will be quite familiar with the quarterback who will be throwing him passes.

The Herberts and the Chargers start the 2026 season on Sept. 13 against the Arizona Cardinals.

articles.title: 49ers Practice Squad Tracker: The potential Week 1 punt returner signs
articles.summary: The 49ers have to cut down to 53 players. But some of those cuts might be sticking around.
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers are starting to make some moves, trimming the 90-man roster to 53. Those that don't make the 53 have a chance of being placed on the practice squad.

The practice squad is important: players on it can travel with the team and do much of the work that any other active player does. They just don't suit up on game day. That means they can help the 49ers prepare for their Week 1 matchup against the Los Angeles Rams.

The 49ers sit as 3.5-point underdogs over at FanDuel Sportsbook . The game is in Melbourne, Australia, with the Rams as the designated home team. Without the Rams' field to help (which usually gets invaded by 49ers fans), the playing field is severely leveled.

An NFL practice squad consists of 17 players. One of which is part of the NFL International Pathway Program, six can be veterans with no cap on experience, and the final 10 must be rookies or second-year players. As of this writing, the full 17 spots are available, so the 49ers have lots of flexibility.

Of that practice squad, the 49ers get to designate four protected players, which means they can't be placed on another team's active roster (basically to stop poaching). Two players can be promoted to the active roster for one week and return to the squad. If they play an additional consecutive week, then the 49ers have to offer the player a one-year deal.

In other words, the 49ers want both young talent they can develop over the season and players who can be absolute backups when injuries occur. Some of these players will be protected and won't even sniff the field for a year while they develop. Others are chances the 49ers take to hold onto unless they sign to another team's active roster.

Isaac Alarcon will be the International Player Pathway exemption following his release, per Matt Maiocco. That allows the 49ers to have 17 on their practice squad.

Maiocco also hinted that running back Khalil Herbert, wide receiver KhaDarel Hodge, and edge rusher Ogbo Okoronkwo would be on the plane for Australia on Wednesday. Whether those are "handshake deals" after being released, or they make the initial 53-man roster remains to be seen.

We'll update this thread in the meantime with any rumors or reports of who the 49ers plan to use to fill out the 17 spots on the squad.

Kyle's update, 9:42 a.m. PT: The Ravens released Adisa Isaac, a former third-round pick from the 2024 NFL Draft.

Isaac has a long list of injuries in his short career. He only played four games as a rookie due to a hamstring injury that lingered into the season after sustaining it during training camp. Last August, Isaac dislocated his elbow in the preseason. That elbow injury cost Isaac his 2025 season after he underwent surgery in November.

Isaac entered the NFL as a raw, toolsy pass rusher. He has elite traits. While he's only listed at around 247 pounds, Isaac had a broad jump in the 83rd percentile, while his height, arm length, 40, and vertical jump were all in the 60th percentile.

The 49ers could buy low on a player like Isaac and hopefully develop him into a role player. Isaac can also contribute on special teams. He'd be a better fit in Raheem Morris's scheme, as Isaac could play from a two-point stance.

The cupboard is bare at the position after Nick Bosa, Mykel Williams, Sam O, and Romello Height. You're unlikely to have Williams healthy to begin the season. Isaac gives you a power rusher who can drop in coverage with traits to build on. Why not roll the dice on a former third-rounder to see if he can give you more than what Ogbo Okoronkwo can?

Kyle's update, 10:59 a.m. PT: A couple of other former draft picks at edge rusher have been waived. Jose Ramirez is undersized, listed at 6'1 7/8″ and 242 pounds. He had elite shuttle times with a 3-cone in the 88th percentile and a 20-yard shuttle in the 78th percentile. If the 49ers are looking to add speed on the roster or practice squad, Ramirez is worth a look.

Trice tore his ACL in the first preseason game of his rookie year. He hurt the same knee last preseason. Injuries are brutal. Some had high hopes for Trice. It's unlikely even Raheem Morris, somebody familiar with Trice, would roll the dice on him after multiple injuries.

Kyle's update, 11:16 a.m. PT: The 49ers released Quinton Bell. That's the first of many moves to come today.

Kyle's update, 12:37 p.m. PT: The 49ers waived tight end Khalil Dinkins. According to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler, the team plans to bring him back to the practice squad if he clears waivers. Dinkins is an intriguing project at tight end. He was an impressive blocker in the preseason finale.

Pat's Update 1:33 p.m PT: The 49ers have waived LB Jalen Graham . That's a possible practice squad candidate. As Matt Barrows points out , Jalen's height + background at safety could be something the 49ers could use.

Pat's Update 1:42 p.m. PT: The 49ers have waived WR Will Pauling . That's another practice squad candidate.

Pat's update 1:50 p.m. PT: Per Matt Maiocco, the 49ers have waived tight end Hayden Rucci . Things are going a bit quicker now as the deadline approaches.

Pat's update 1:51 p.m. PT: The 49ers have waived defensive back Patrick McMorris. That's another practice squad candidate.

Kyle's update, 2:15 p.m. PT : Jalen Stroman has been waived, per Maiocco. The 49ers intend to bring him back to the practice squad.

Kyle's update, 2:57 p.m. PT: Any minute now, the 49ers' full roster should be out. Until then, the team released wide receiver KhaDarel Hodge. Depending on how they feel about the rest of the receiver room, Hodge would be a candidate to return to the practice squad and be elevated on game day to cover kicks.

Kyle's update, Monday, 10:36 a.m. PT: The 49ers are building their practice squad. According to Matt Barrows, edge rusher Ogbo Okoronkwo, tight end Khalil Dinkins, and wide receiver Wesley Grimes will all sign with the practice squad.

Kyle's update, 11:17 a.m. PT: Linebacker Jalen Graham and defensive tackle Sebastian Valdez will also join the practice squad, according to Barrows.

Mike Garafolo tweeted that wide receiver Will Pauling will also join the practice squad.

Vic Tafur tweeted that running back Sincere McCormick will also sign to the practice squad. That brings the practice squad to 7 members.

Pat's update 12:07 p.m. PT : For those of you hoping to see Darrell Luter or Bryson Eason coming to the 49ers practice squad, you will be disappoited. Both have been claimed off waivers. Easeon was claimed by the Kansas City Chiefs and Darrell Luter was claimed by the Las Vegas Raiders.

Pat's Update 12:31 p.m. PT: 49ers have announced their practice squad signings. In addition to the ones we've updated it looks like KhaDarel Hodge, Drake Nugent, Ogbo Okoronkwo, Jakob Robinson, Jalen Stroman, and Jon Weeks are officially official for the squad. Here's the list: OT – Isaac Alarcon TE – Khalil Dinkins LB – Jalen Graham WR – Wesley Grimes WR – KhaDarel Hodge RB – Sincere McCormick OL – Drake Nugent DL – Ogbo Okoronkwo WR – Will Pauling CB – Jakob Robinson S – Jalen Stroman DL – Sebastian Valdez LS – Jon Weeks

Pat's Update 12:36 p.m. PT: It's never done. In addition to the above names, Matt Barrows reports the 49ers plan to sign OL Foster Sarell to the practice squad.

Kyle's update, 4:16 p.m. PT: Former Bills cornerback Brandon Codrington signed to the practice squad, per Aaron Wilson.

Codrington spent the past two seasons with the Buffalo Bills. He was undrafted in the 2024 NFL Draft. Codrington, 5'9″, 180 pounds, played sparingly in the slot for Buffalo. He did get some action as a kick and punt returner. His longest return came in Week 1 of last season. That was 41 yards. He also had a couple of double-digit-yard punt returns.

As a rookie, Codrington had a 53-yard kickoff return in Week 1 against the Cardinals. He had four punt returns of at least 20 yards. With Jacob Cowing working on the side of practice Monday, this might be the team's punt returner in Week 1

articles.title: Inspiring story on women’s empowerment: "Women don’t just have a seat at the table, but they own the building that the table sits in"- How Brittany Mahomes is redefining what female leadership means
articles.summary: NFL News: Brittany Mahomes put women’s empowerment at the centre of her message when she accepted United WE’s inaugural Champion for Change Award at CPKC Stadiu.
articles.body: Brittany Mahomes put women’s empowerment at the centre of her message when she accepted United WE’s inaugural Champion for Change Award at CPKC Stadium in Kansas City on May 6, 2026. Speaking during the organisation’s 35th anniversary celebration, the Kansas City Current co-owner called for a future where women do more than occupy influential positions. She urged them to build, lead and create the spaces where decisions are made.Brittany Mahomes’ powerful words about women’s empowermentMahomes used her acceptance speech to explain what meaningful progress for women should look like. Her message went beyond simply encouraging women to pursue opportunities. She focused on creating lasting change and giving women greater control over the spaces they enter.She said:“We are here to build real equity and create spaces where women don’t just have a seat at the table, but they own the building that the table sits in,”The statement stood out because of the distinction Mahomes made between having a place in an existing system and having the power to shape that system.For her, representation is only the beginning. Women should also have the opportunity to become owners, decision-makers and leaders.The setting added another layer to her message. Mahomes delivered the remarks at CPKC Stadium, the home of the Kansas City Current, the National Women's Soccer League team she co-owns. The stadium itself has become a prominent symbol of investment in women’s professional sports.That made her words about ownership particularly fitting.CPKC Stadium reflects Brittany Mahomes’ visionThe choice of venue was significant. CPKC Stadium was built specifically for a women’s professional sports team, creating a permanent home for the Kansas City Current.Mahomes has played a role in the club's ownership group alongside her husband, Patrick Mahomes, and other investors. Her involvement has also given her a platform to speak about the growth of women’s sports and the importance of investing in them.Kimmi Chex, who hosted the United WE event, highlighted the connection between Mahomes and the stadium.“The event here today was built in the stadium that Brittany Mahomes built herself,” Chex said. “CPKC is a stadium that really was her vision and was her voice and also her funding.”The comments underlined why Mahomes’ message resonated so strongly at the event. She was speaking about ownership from a venue that represents a major investment in women’s sport.The achievement also reflects how the conversation around women’s athletics has evolved. Women’s sports are no longer being discussed only in terms of participation or visibility. Investment, ownership, infrastructure and long-term growth have become equally important parts of the discussion.Brittany Mahomes wants women to redefine successMahomes also spoke about the example women can set for younger generations.She has built a public identity that stretches across several areas, including sports, business and motherhood. Rather than presenting these roles as competing parts of her life, she encouraged women to view ambition and family as things that can exist together.“I want them to grow up in a world where women owning a team or a company is the standard,” Mahomes said.She continued:“And I want them to know that being a mother and an athlete, an entrepreneur, or whatever they want to be, isn’t just a balancing act. It is a power move.”The message is especially relevant in professional sports, where women have historically faced greater barriers to ownership and leadership.Mahomes' comments suggest that the next stage of women’s empowerment should involve changing expectations. A woman should not have to explain why she wants to lead a company, own a sports team or pursue a demanding career while raising a family.Instead, those ambitions should be viewed as normal.Brittany Mahomes honoured for her workUnited WE recognised Mahomes with its inaugural Champion for Change Award during its 35th anniversary celebration. The organisation praised her work as an entrepreneur, investor, athlete, mother and co-owner of the Kansas City Current.United WE president and CEO Wendy Doyle explained why Mahomes was selected for the honour.“She is a very independent woman who is really making significant change and using her influence to really impact the sports industry and beyond,” Doyle said. “We couldn’t think of a better person to recognize.”Doyle also used the occasion to point to the growing business potential of women’s sports.“This stadium sends a clear message. Women’s sports are not a cause. They are a market,” said Doyle. “And when you invest in them, they grow.”That idea closely connects with Mahomes’ own comments about ownership. Building opportunities requires more than visibility. It requires people willing to invest money, time and influence into creating something that can last.The event also brought attention to the broader challenges women continue to face. From childcare costs to workplace inequality, many of the barriers are rooted in systems rather than a lack of ambition.Shelley Zalis, founder and CEO of The Female Quotient, captured that argument with another memorable statement:“Women aren’t broken. It’s fixing the system,” Zalis said.Mahomes’ speech fits naturally into that wider conversation. Her message was not simply about encouraging women to work harder or fight for a place in an established hierarchy.It was about changing the hierarchy itself.Her words at CPKC Stadium offered a clear vision of what that future could look like. Women should not have to settle for being invited into rooms where major decisions are made. They should have the opportunity to build those rooms, own them and decide who gets a seat.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Chad Ochocinco warns Browns' Deshaun Watson has 'very short' leash, could lose starting job by Week 3
articles.summary: Chad Ochocinco said Deshaun Watson's leash is "very short" and predicts the Browns will make a move if Cleveland starts the 2026 NFL season 0-2.
articles.body: The Cleveland Browns made their quarterback decision entering the 2026 NFL season, but football fans are still trying to process why Deshaun Watson is getting the Week 1 start against the Jacksonville Jaguars over Shedeur Sanders. The decision by first-year head coach Todd Monken may have answered the question on everyone’s mind for the Browns this preseason, but the debate still rages on throughout the football world considering Watson’s track record in Cleveland and how the $230 million man hasn’t lived up to his contract in the slightest. In fact, fans booed Watson during their home preseason against the Buffalo Bills, to which he called them "disrespectful" and "personal" rather than a reaction to his performance on the field. CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM Either way, Watson heads into the new campaign – his first regular-season play since tearing his Achilles in 2024 – with an immense amount of pressure. However, one former NFL star believes the leash will be quite tight for the veteran signal caller. Maybe to the point where he doesn’t start under center come Week 3 – the Browns’ home opener against the Carolina Panthers. "If they start the season 0-2 – you open with the Jaguars. Then, you have Tampa Bay, then you come home. I’m not sure you play the third game, but you’d have to start that season off either 1-1 or 2-0. Either 1-1 or 2-0. One or the other. If you start off 0-2, they’re making a move. They’re making a move before the season gets too far away from them," Chad Ochocinco told OutKick in a recent interview while highlighting his partnership with DraftKings ahead of this NFL season. DESHAUN WATSON SAYS 'EMOTIONS GOT THE BEST OF ME' AFTER RIPPING CLEVELAND BROWNS FANS FOR BOOING Ochocinco has been very vocal about the Browns’ quarterback conundrum on his "Nightcap" podcast with Shannon Sharpe, where he’s noted on numerous occasions that there was never really a position battle between Watson, Sanders, Dillon Gabriel and anyone else on the quarterbacks' depth chart. "It was never a quarterback competition. It never was. At no point in any game is the $46 million man competing for a job and would lose to the younger player based on salary," Ochocinco said. "As an owner and person writing the check, Deshaun Watson was always going to be the starting quarterback no matter what. Now, it’s his job to lose now going forward, and his leash is going to be very short." From the fan perspective, Ochocinco also understands why the Browns faithful feel the way they do about Watson. Since he came over in a now-infamous trade with the Houston Texans, Watson, who was given a whopping $230 million, fully guaranteed contract over five years, has started just 19 games across three seasons, with injuries and his lengthy 11-game NFL suspension coming in 2022. In those games, the Browns have gone 9-10, including the most recent in 2024 where he went 1-6. Watson has thrown 19 touchdowns compared to 12 interceptions, competing 61.2% of his passes for 3,365 yards and a passer rating of 80.7. For comparison there, in his four years with the Texans, where he earned three Pro Bowls and led the NFL with 4,823 yards in 2020, he had a passer rating of 104.5. "The fans are upset, the fans are booing because they have nothing to cheer for," Ochocinco said. "You haven’t given them anything to cheer for in general. So, the bad taste that’s left in their mouths are the issues that came with you from Houston on top of coming here to Cleveland. You’ve given them nothing to cheer for, therefore that’s why they’re gonna feel the way they feel." So, what do Watson and the Browns do if even their home crowd seems to be against the most important player on the field for them come Week 1? As the saying goes, the shortest way through a storm is straight. Watson is going to have to face the music, and Ochocinco is hoping he can do it. HALL OF FAMER JOE THOMAS ON SKIPPING THE NFL DRAFT TO FISH, RAISING WAGYU AND TRANSFORMING HIS HEALTH "But one thing can happen: performing and winning cures all," he said. "Listen, they come out the gate, somehow find a way to beat Jacksonville, find a way to beat Tampa, and you go into Cleveland the first home game 2-0. Man, they will cheer their a—off. You’re gonna hear cheering and eruptions of cheering for Deshaun that he’s never heard before. Honestly, I’m hoping he does. "Winning cures all. It doesn’t matter what you did. You’re the quarterback of their team. If you start out the gate 1-1 at best – 2-0 best scenario – they’re going to love you in Cleveland despite what you’ve done. They’ll love you because you’re winning – something they haven’t had consistently for a very long time." It will be a tough task for Watson and the Browns to get those wins against playoff hopefuls in Weeks 1 and 2. But Ochocinco sees no other way for Watson to hang on to his job even if it is just the start of a new campaign. OCHO LOVES DRAFTKINGS GAMEDAY College football is already underway, and the NFL is right around the corner, which has Ochocinco very excited about football being back. Also, he’s excited to impact the fan experience with DraftKings. "DraftKings Gameday," which will take place on Sept. 2, was announced on Monday with quite the activation as it celebrates the first football season with DraftKings Sports & Casino available in all 50 states. As a way to fuel fans with the return of football, DraftKings will be offering free gas, while supplies last, to passenger vehicles at select gas stations in Los Angeles, Miami, Dallas, Atlanta and Detroit. Specific locations and event times will be announced separately. "For me, I think it’s fun because who else would do something like this outside of DraftKings. This is a great touch for NFL fans to start the season," Ochocinco said. "We’re giving you free gas, so when your respective team plays, you’re fueled up to go. And word of mouth will be, ‘You won’t believe this? You know what DraftKings did? I was able to save money and get tickets to go to a game because they paid for my gas.’ That makes sense." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP There will also be exclusive DraftKings Gameday promotions for customers, a customized in-app experience, in-person activations, a charitable donation through the DraftKings SERVES program, and a new campaign featuring Kevin Hart and Nick Jonas this season. "It’s all about the fan experience, so some of the offers and luxuries throughout the season is what sets us apart from everybody else. I’m happy to be a part of them," Ochocinco said.

articles.title: Colin Kaepernick’s 10-year journey from NFL star to a lasting symbol of athlete activism and social change
articles.summary: NFL News: Colin Kaepernick was still an NFL quarterback when he began a protest that would follow him long after his football career ended. In 2016, he refused .
articles.body: Colin Kaepernick was still an NFL quarterback when he began a protest that would follow him long after his football career ended. In 2016, he refused to stand for the national anthem to draw attention to racial injustice and police brutality. Ten years later, the image of Kaepernick on one knee remains closely connected with athlete activism across American sports.The protest began quietly during the San Francisco 49ers’ preseason. Kaepernick eventually lost his place in the NFL, but athletes in several major sports later used similar gestures and public platforms to address social issues. Colin Kaepernick’s 2016 protest quickly moved beyond the NFLKaepernick first sat during the anthem before San Francisco’s preseason game against the Houston Texans on August 14, 2016. He did the same against the Denver Broncos on August 20, but few people noticed because he did not play in either game.That changed after a few days, when Kaepernick sat during the anthem before playing against the Green Bay Packers. After the game, he explained his decision to NFL reporter Steve Wyche.“I am not going to stand up to show pride in a flag for a country that oppresses Black people and people of color,” Kaepernick told Wyche after the Packers game.Kaepernick had also spoken publicly about the deaths of Alton Sterling and Philando Castile, two Black men killed by police in July 2016. Their deaths came only weeks before his first visible protest.After speaking with former NFL player and retired Green Beret Nate Boyer, Kaepernick changed his approach from sitting to kneeling. On September 1, 2016, he knelt beside teammate Eric Reid before the 49ers played the San Diego Chargers.The response grew quickly. Kaepernick received boos and death threats, while then-Republican presidential candidate Donald Trump criticized his decision during the 2016 campaign.Other athletes soon joined the conversation. Soccer star Megan Rapinoe knelt during the anthem in support of Kaepernick. NBA teams linked arms during the anthem, while WNBA players also staged protests.During the 2017 WNBA Finals, the Los Angeles Sparks stayed in the locker room during the anthem, while the Minnesota Lynx linked arms before Game 1. Former WNBA star Diana Taurasi later said athletes wanted Kaepernick to know that “we have his back.” Kaepernick lost his NFL career but continued his work outside footballKaepernick continued playing throughout the 2016 season, starting 11 games for San Francisco and finishing with 2,241 passing yards, 16 touchdowns and four interceptions. He also rushed for 468 yards and two touchdowns.His final NFL appearance came on January 1, 2017, against the Seattle Seahawks. He became a free agent after the season and never played another NFL game.Kaepernick and Reid later filed grievances against the NFL, alleging that team owners colluded to keep them out of the league. The sides reached a confidential settlement on February 15, 2019.Kaepernick still pursued a return. On May 25, 2022, he worked out for the Las Vegas Raiders, but the team did not sign him.His work away from football continued through his Know Your Rights Camp, which focuses on education, self-empowerment and community engagement. His activism also remained visible during the nationwide protests that followed George Floyd’s death in May 2020.The NFL eventually acknowledged its own handling of player protests. In June 2020, Commissioner Roger Goodell said the league should have listened more closely to players who raised concerns about racial injustice.Now, as September 1, 2026 marks 10 years since Kaepernick first knelt beside Reid, his football career remains frozen in 2017. His activism has continued for a decade, giving his story a place far beyond the NFL.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Travis Hunter Will 'Absolutely' Have a Role on Offense amid 2-Way Questions, Jaguars HC Says
articles.summary: Travis Hunter's role as a two-way player has been in question this offseason, but Jacksonville Jaguars head coach Liam Coen clarified that he'll continue to play on both sides of the ball.
articles.body:
Travis Hunter's role as a two-way player has been in question this offseason, but Jacksonville Jaguars head coach Liam Coen clarified that he'll continue to play on both sides of the ball.

"Absolutely. We'll definitely have a package on offense to be able to get him some opportunities," Coen said on the Rich Eisen Show (7:45 mark). "There's been a steady increase in his defensive work just by nature of where we're at on defense and continuing to try to create consistency... There's been a lot of detail and time-on-task this offseason. He'll absolutely have a plan on offense. "

Hunter won the Heisman Trophy at Colorado because of his tremendous play on both sides of the ball, but many fairly assumed that he'd have to pick one or the other once he got to the NFL.

That wasn't the case during his rookie year, though, as he recorded 28 receptions for 298 yards and a touchdown while racking up 15 tackles and three passes defended on defense in seven games.

After the season, a few reports indicated that Hunter would pivot to mostly playing corner while getting a few snaps at wide receiver. He questioned those reports on social media.

The extent of Hunter's role on offense and defense remains to be seen, but he's proved that he's capable of playing at a high level on both sides of the ball.

articles.title: “It was definitely unfortunate”: CeeDee Lamb breaks silence after $300K home burglary as Cowboys star turns focus back to 2026 season
articles.summary: NFL News: CeeDee Lamb has finally spoken about the burglary at his Fairview, Texas, home. The Dallas Cowboys receiver was away at training camp in California wh.
articles.body: CeeDee Lamb has finally spoken about the burglary at his Fairview, Texas, home. The Dallas Cowboys receiver was away at training camp in California when the break-in happened on July 30. Thieves reportedly took more than $300,000 worth of belongings, including four luxury bags.Nearly a month later, Lamb addressed the incident for the first time. He kept his response brief but admitted the situation was unfortunate. Now, with the Cowboys preparing for the 2026 season, Lamb appears ready to leave the incident behind. CeeDee Lamb addresses the burglary after returning from Cowboys campThe burglary happened while Lamb was with the Cowboys at their training camp in Oxnard, California. According to police, a burglar broke a window at the Fairview home and used the same opening to get inside and leave.The break-in came to light on July 31, when a worker at Lamb’s property noticed the damaged window and contacted police. Investigators later determined that several valuable items had disappeared. The reported losses exceeded $300,000, with four luxury bags among the stolen belongings.There was no indication that Lamb or anyone else was inside the home when the burglary happened. Police also had not identified a suspect in the latest reports.CeeDee Lamb finally addressed the matter after returning from California. According to Fort Worth Star-Telegram reporter Nick Harris, the Cowboys wide receiver said, “It was definitely unfortunate. Things like that happen. Gotta be better. For sure. For sure.”His response was short, but the timing matters. Lamb spent much of the summer away from home with Dallas, and the burglary happened during that stretch. The incident also comes amid a string of home burglaries involving professional athletes. Cowboys receiver CeeDee Lamb has bigger goals after difficult 2025 seasonCeeDee Lamb now has plenty to focus on as the Dallas Cowboys moves toward the regular season. He finished 2025 with 75 catches for 1,077 yards and three touchdowns in 14 games.However, his season also included eight drops. That number pushed Lamb to work differently during Cowboys training camp.He used a JUGS machine while wearing a covering over his head that limited his vision. The unusual drill forced him to concentrate harder while tracking the football.That work reflects what CeeDee Lamb wants from 2026. He remains one of the Dallas Cowboys’ most important offensive players and has already recorded five 1,000-yard seasons in his first six NFL years.The burglary gave Lamb an unwanted problem away from football. Still, his response suggests he does not plan to let it become a distraction.For now, the Dallas Cowboys receiver has addressed what happened. His attention has shifted back to catching passes, improving his game and helping Dallas start the 2026 season on the right foot.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.summary: College football’s newest eligibility fight gave Steve Sarkisian a chance to draw a moral line on Monday. Fans immediately started checking the Texas roster.
articles.body:
College football's newest eligibility fight gave Steve Sarkisian a chance to draw a moral line on Monday. Fans immediately started checking the Texas roster.

The Longhorns coach criticized cutting a college player who spent the offseason with the program simply to make room for someone coming directly from an NFL roster. However, the return of veteran Texas offensive lineman Cole Hutson made that position an instant target.

Steve Sarkisian's Moral Argument Gets Immediate Pushback

"The fact that somebody out there is going to take a player off of an NFL roster and tell somebody who's been doing it for nine months to go kick rocks, that doesn't sit well with me," Sarkisian said on Monday . "I think that's wrong. That, morally, is wrong."

"He literally did the exact same thing," the user wrote in an X response .

Another fan questioned Sarkisian's broader image.

"Sark being the nice guy is the biggest lie ever told," the user wrote in another X post .

"Coach who has a player off a nfl roster complaining about players off of nfl rosters HYPOCRITE," another fan wrote in an X reply .

One user asked , "Umm, did he kick Cole Hutson off the team?"

"Sark talking about morals? Pot meet kettle," another fan added.

PREDICT THE CFB SEASON: PFN's Free CFB Playoff Predictor

While fans were quick to call Sarkisian a hypocrite, it's worth noting that Hutson was never actually on an NFL roster.

The former Texas starter went undrafted and participated in rookie minicamps with the Dallas Cowboys and Cleveland Browns, but he did not sign an NFL contract. After suing the NCAA, Hutson regained a fifth season and officially rejoined Texas in August. Sarkisian had previously distinguished Hutson from the NFL returnees controversy because he had already spent four years inside the Longhorns program.

That differs from the cases driving the current debate, including former NFL signees attempting to come back to college after being released. The SEC tried to prohibit such returns before a Louisiana court temporarily blocked enforcement, with another hearing scheduled Thursday.

Sarkisian's specific objection on Monday was narrower still. He objected to removing someone who had been with a college team for nine months to accommodate a player arriving at the last minute from an NFL roster. There is no verified evidence that Texas cut a player to make room for Hutson.

Texas is trying to maximize a championship-caliber roster. The Longhorns went 10-3 last season, while they ranked 17th nationally in PFN's Defense Impact Score with a 85.4 grade and 38th nationally in PFN's Offense Impact Score with a 79.7 grade.

With Sarkisian condemning late NFL additions while welcoming back a player who spent his spring pursuing the league, fans were going to have something to say. However, the details make the two situations less identical than the "HYPOCRITE" claim suggests.

In college football's current eligibility mess, nuance has rarely been the part that goes viral.

articles.title: “Sam Howell Is Trash”: NFL Legend Rips Cowboys for Cutting Joe Milton From 53-Man Roster
articles.summary: On Monday, August 31, the Dallas Cowboys had to make some tough decisions. They decided to keep Sam Howell as the quarterback behind Dak Prescott.
articles.body:
On Monday, August 31, the Dallas Cowboys had to make some tough decisions. They decided to keep Sam Howell as the quarterback behind Dak Prescott. This move did not sit well with Roddy White, who took a stand for preseason standout Joe Milton, who was cut from the 53-man roster.

"How the hell joe Milton get cut he literally dominated the whole preseason," the former Atlanta Falcons wide receiver wrote on X on Monday. "Sam Howell is trash like dumpster trash."

Dallas initially moved forward with a three-quarterback plan on their initial 53-man roster on Sunday. However, the next day, they waived Milton in order to make space for running back Emari Demercado, whom the Cowboys signed after he was waived by the Kansas City Chiefs.

The 26-year-old Milton arrived in Dallas last year via a trade with the New England Patriots. He played in four games, recording 183 passing yards, one touchdown, and two interceptions. Milton then turned heads during the 2026 preseason, completing 29 of 43 attempts for 378 yards, three touchdowns, and no interceptions.

Definitely, his efficiency made him a strong contender in the QB2 race. But ultimately, the Cowboys chose Howell, whose last-game heroics in the preseason finale against the New Orleans Saints might have pushed his case.

Howell initially struggled after halftime, going three-and-out on his first third-quarter drive, which ended with a sack. But he answered with a massive 52-yard completion to Jordan Hudson. On the first play of the fourth quarter, he followed it with a 26-yard touchdown pass to Hudson and then led a 12-play, 67-yard drive capped by Mitch Van Voren's 21-yard touchdown. Howell added the two-point conversion himself, tying the game.

Milton, however, was broadly expected to win the QB2 race after his preseason performance. For instance, Asante Samuel had put Milton on a pedestal.

"The Dallas Cowboys are gonna end up winning the NFC East. It's just my prediction. I still expect them to be that good if Joe Milton does end up having to take over for some unfortunate reason, some unfortunate circumstances," Samuel shared on his podcast, "Say What Needs to be Said". "That probably will increase the Cowboys' chances of getting further in the playoffs. It's just another way of saying Joe Milton III brings more to the table than Dak Prescott."

Milton also attracted comparisons to Cam Newton from Saints guest coach Nicholas Williams during their joint practice.

While Roddy White is upset with the Cowboys' move, Star Telegram's Nick Harris finds a silver lining in the timing.

"I'm chalking up the timing of the Joe Milton III release to roster/waiver strategy," he wrote on X. "Release him on Sunday, much higher chance he gets claimed. Release him today, a lot of teams have their QB situations figured out, making it more likely he clears waivers. Just my take."

Per ESPN, the Cowboys explored trade opportunities for Milton before Sunday's 53-man roster deadline. Should he clear waivers, Dallas could re-sign him to the practice squad, but it remains uncertain whether the team will pursue that option.

Meanwhile, the Cowboys were in a tough spot. Howell had a $2.5 million guaranteed contract. In case they chose the route of releasing the quarterback, they would still owe him his $2 million base salary. Even by placing him on the practice squad, the salary obligation would still apply because his money was guaranteed.

That's why they thought of compromising and waived Milton.

Because Milton has not achieved vested veteran status in his third season, he is subject to waivers rather than free agency. If no other team claims him, Dallas gets to keep him on its practice squad.
